title: Onboarding Fidelity SLA and Noise Budget Manifest
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Summary
This manifest defines the end-to-end onboarding criteria for new model artifacts and model variants with an explicit fidelity SLA and a quantifiable noise budget. The goal is to provide a single operational contract teams must satisfy to promote a model from shadow to canary and finally to production serving (hosted, dedicated, or private). This document covers: fidelity SLOs, noise budget accounting, telemetry contract, quantization interaction rules, prompt-set acceptance, and regression triage triggers.

Motivation and scope
- Problem: Model promotions are often blocked or reversed because quality regressions are discovered post-rollout; however, teams lack a concise SLA and a standard noise accounting system to decide trade-offs between performance, cost (quantization), and latency.
- Scope: Applies to all model-onboarding flows for text/chat/embedding services. Multimodal extensions are optional and covered in the appendix.

Key definitions
1) Fidelity SLA: A measurable target that constrains allowable delta in signal for prioritized slices (see Slice Matrix). Example: "Per-slice fidelity delta <= 3% absolute on primary metric OR delta <= 0.02 AUC on rerankers".
2) Noise budget: A bounded allocation of allowable false positives and metric variance for a rollout window (default: 30 days). Expressed as: allowable_misclassifications_per_100k_requests and/or allowable_stddev_increase.
3) Slice: A workload partition with well-defined traffic, importance weight, and primary metric (e.g., enterprise-api:prompt_type=code_completion, primary_metric=token_coherence).
4) Quant-fitness: A model variant's acceptable quantization level defined via quality delta margins and latency/cost improvements.

High-level promotion gates
- Shadow -> Canary: unit-eval pass AND shadow telemetry within 60% of slice noise budget AND quant-fitness validated for intended quant profile.
- Canary -> Prod: canary telemetry steady for 72 hours, max slice fidelity delta under the per-slice SLA, cumulative noise spent <= allocated budget, no critical quality sentinel alerts.
- Prod pin -> rollback: automatic rollback if an SLO breach occurs with high confidence (see Escalation & Rollback).

Fidelity SLA manifest (table)
(plaintext table; rows separated by pipes)
| Slice ID | Traffic % | Primary metric | Baseline | SLA delta | Noise budget (30d) |
| enterprise-code | 12% | token_coherence@50k | 0.842 | <=0.015 absolute | 120 misclassifications per 100k |
| consumer-chat | 48% | answer_acceptance_rate | 0.913 | <=0.01 absolute | 220 misclassifications per 100k |
| low-volume-legal | 3% | factuality_precision | 0.78 | <=0.02 absolute | 8 misclassifications per 100k |

Telemetry contract (minimal required fields)
- Ingest frequency: 1 event per response (default).
- Fields per event: request_id, slice_id, model_variant, quant_profile, latency_ms, token_count, primary_metric_value, sentinel_flags, timestamp, error_code (if any).
- Aggregation windows: 5m (fast), 1h (stability), 24h (trend).
- Retention: metrics 90 days aggregated; raw events 30 days.

Alerting and sentinels
- Severity P0: Critical fidelity breach (slice delta > 2x SLA and p<0.01), auto-rollback and page SRE team + model owner.
- Severity P1: Noise budget exhaustion threshold (>= 80% spent), email + Slack to model owner and product manager, create triage ticket.
- Severity P2: Latency regression > 25% vs baseline for 3 consecutive 5m windows.

Noise budget accounting (procedures)
1) Convert observed metric deltas into budget units: the team must store a conversion map that defines "budget units" per metric delta (example: 1 misclassification = 1 unit; 0.001 absolute drop in answer_acceptance_rate = 0.5 units).
2) Per-window accounting: compute units spent per 5m window and sum for the rolling 30d window.
3) Replenishment and transfer: budgets replenish monthly at 30d cadence; limited transfer allowed between sibling slices under approval.

Quantization interaction rules
- Default requirement: any quant profile that reduces memory or latency by >6% must run a dedicated quant-shadow with the full slice matrix for >= 24h and consume <= 40% of the noise budget during that test.
- Mixed-precision rollout: allowed if per-token coherence delta <= SLA and tail-latency unchanged within 10%.
- Reversible artifacting: keep float32 artifact of each promoted variant for at least 14 days to allow deterministic replay for regression triage.

Onboarding checklist (step-by-step)
1) Prepare artifacts: model_variant_id, weights URI, quant_profile(s), inference config YAML.
2) Register slice manifest: list slices and primary metrics in the onboarding PR.
3) Unit & automated evals: run eval harness coverage (functional, toxic, bias, rerank) and attach evaluation report. Pass threshold: all critical tests green.
4) Shadow run: route 100% duplicate traffic to shadow mode for 48h, collect telemetry. Ensure noise spent <= 60% for each critical slice.
5) Canary deploy: route 1–5% traffic via canary policy with progressive ramp for 72h. Monitor alerts and budget.
6) Review and sign-off: model owner, applied-ml reviewer, and SRE sign-off in the PR.
7) Promote to prod with pinned rollout policy and rollback window (default 14 days).

Example YAML: fidelity SLA (snippet)
---
model_variant: rwd-new-3b-quant128
baseline_snapshot: snapshot-2026-01-12
slices:
  - id: enterprise-code
    primary_metric: token_coherence@50k
    baseline: 0.842
    allowed_delta: 0.015
    noise_budget_30d: 120
quant_profile: q128-mixed
telemetry_endpoint: /v1/internal/telemetry/events
---

Operational queries (examples)
- 5-min slice delta: SELECT slice_id, AVG(primary_metric_value) AS avg_m, COUNT(*) AS N FROM telemetry.events WHERE model_variant='rwd-new-3b-quant128' AND ts >= now() - interval '5 minutes' GROUP BY slice_id;
- Noise budget spent (30d): SELECT slice_id, SUM(budget_units) FROM telemetry.budget_spends WHERE model_variant='rwd-new-3b-quant128' AND ts >= now() - interval '30 days' GROUP BY slice_id;

Escalation and rollback playbook
1) Auto-detect: monitoring system raises P0 -> automatic gradual traffic re-route to last-known-good variant (5-step, 50% increments) while alerting SRE and model owner.
2) Triage timeline: initial triage 30m, full RCA within 72h. If RCA indicates training/data-change, escalate to Applied ML and Data platform.
3) Regression triage checklist: reproduce via float replay; run core eval suite; check quant shadow logs and KV cache mismatch metrics; check prompt-set sensitivity for anchors.

Ownership and SLAs
- Model owner: responsible for onboarding artifacts, sign-offs, and first-level triage.
- Applied ML: responsible for the eval harness integration and evaluation report integrity.
- SRE: responsible for telemetry, alerting, and auto-rollback tooling.
- Product: approves acceptable fidelity trade-offs for slices they own.

Versioning and audit
- Every promoted variant must include an immutable manifest (S3 URI) that contains: model_hash, artifact_list, eval_reports, quant_snapshot, slice_manifest, and noise_budget_state.
- Audit events generated on: shadow_start, shadow_end, canary_start, canary_end, promote, rollback. Stored in audit-log/onnboarding-events for 1 year.

Appendix: guidance for common scenarios
- Small-sample slices: use bootstrapped confidence intervals for delta estimation; downweight their noise budgets by factor 0.5 if traffic <0.5% to avoid noisy overreactions.
- Cost-critical customers: for dedicated/private tenants requesting aggressive quantization, create a separate per-tenant budget and require product signoff.
- Multimodal note: image-text slices should include per-modality fidelity metrics and per-modality quant checks.
